the mechanisms that govern the recognition of protein substrates by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
understanding the molecular basis for the recognition of the N-terminal residues of proteins and the subsequent polyubiquitylations that target these proteins for degradation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ubiquitin-proteasome system is the most complex, dynamic, and versatile proteolytic machinery known to date.
the ubiquitin system has a single pathway for targeting substrates for proteolysis.
the N-end rule is a component of the UFD pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-end rule is a ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
Ubr1 is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that can function in two distinct proteolytic systems.
the N-end rule E3 enzyme, Ubr1, and the UFD E3 enzyme, the Ufd4, together constitute an N-end rule pathway that targets a wide variety of substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ubiquitin system is highly flexible and can adapt to different cellular needs.
ubiquitylation by the N-end rule is not an isolated process.
the ubiquitylation of substrates is not a binary event, but rather a dynamic process that can be regulated in a number of ways, and that these processes are not restricted to the proteasome.
